GTP is a new quantitative study of an existing runtime: its older documentation and software are separated from newly disclosed GB300 scaling, training and matched-comparison evidence. entries.title: DAiSy: Online Data Selection by Adaptive Utility Estimation for LLM Pretraining
summary: DAiSy learns a lightweight online document scorer from gradient-alignment labels collected during training, avoiding full model passes over rejected candidates.

Across 124M and 720M pretraining runs, target-guided selection improves benchmark performance and token efficiency; measured runtime overhead and losses on general web data make the target and selection window important practical choices.

evidence.rationale: Independently read main pp.1–15 and all scientific Appendices A–I pp.19–36; reference-only pp.16–18 were not independently audited. Directly viewed actual Table1 p.8, cost Table4 p.21, equal-compute Figure12 p.22 and multilingual Table7/Figure23 p.32. DAiSy refreshes a target-gradient direction every200 steps and collects first-order Adam-preconditioned document-gradient alignment labels from ordinary selected-document backward passes every4 steps. A frozen-embedding online ridge scorer uses Gaussianized rank labels, decayed sufficient statistics and a candidate window to select documents without full LLM passes on rejected candidates. English124M/720M models train for33.6B tokens with single seeds; at candidate factor16 and a five-benchmark training-split target, the mean zero-shot accuracy over eight tasks is46.93/53.77% versus uniform43.22/49.01%. A separate educational-web target can improve over uniform FineWeb-Edu, and multilingual and token-limited studies expose target imbalance/repetition effects. Table4 reports32.6–43.4 GPU-hours versus28.8 for uniform at124M, while measured step-time ratios are1.13–1.51 and peak allocated memory rises from16.2GiB to about21–22GiB; its per-GPU caption does not reconcile directly with the stated step counts, so the GPU-hour values are attributed rather than independently scope-verified. The claimed5.6% arithmetic overhead is not measured wall-time overhead, and the7.6x/4.7x token-efficiency crossings apply to matching the final uniform target loss, not total pipeline speedups. v1 receipt is November24 09:54:25UTC despite the cover date November25. Original LG NEW/dated RECENT and the official schedule support inferred announcement November25 01:00UTC. The linked GitHub project, repository API, commit endpoint and raw README all returned404; no code/project link is presented as verified.
evidence.limitations: Every pretraining configuration is a single seed and the models are small. Task-directed improvements can sacrifice general FineWeb likelihood; multilingual benchmark targeting can overfit Chinese and harm other languages. Target construction, candidate window, selector memory and redundancy penalties matter, so no universal data-quality ranking follows. The scorer learns from selected documents and stale periodically refreshed target directions, not unbiased exact causal utilities for every candidate. Precomputed whole-corpus embeddings add upstream storage/compute that is not quantified in the displayed training-cost comparison. Main hardware descriptions differ between GH200 configuration wording and H200 cost-table wording; no hardware-specific global throughput claim is made. The multilingual124M block configuration actually has238.6M total parameters after its larger vocabulary. Some target-document counts differ between main text and appendix; those counts are not relied on here. Held-out benchmark splits and hash exclusion are described by authors, not independently audited contamination removal. Author implementation is currently inaccessible; no code or experiment was executed.

entries.title: Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers
summary: UDV-Rebalance inserts diagonal scale buffers between paired Transformer weights and restores their factors to fixed norms after every update.

A recipe calibrated on small vision models transfers to 120M–1.3B language pretraining without per-model sweeps, offering a practical starting point for reducing tuning while wider-model stability failures show its limits.

evidence.rationale: New reparameterization and deployment study, distinct from the previously covered analysis of existing optimizer memory. Independently read main pp.1–12 and all scientific Appendices A–F pp.15–32; reference-only pp.13–14 were not independently audited. Directly viewed Figure3 p.11, wider-model Figure11 p.28 and configurations/results Tables21–23 p.32. UDVR adds a non-gradient diagonal buffer D between paired U,V matrices, fixes each U-column/V-row norm to alpha*sqrt(d), and uses shape-dependent learning rates plus a scale regularizer. Linear/attention rebalancing preserves UDV, whereas the operational GELU/SiLU FFN rule absorbs only the U scale and discards V scale; it is not an exact function-preserving transformation there. One-off small-vision characterization selects alpha=.01, gamma=1e-7 and C=.0217, then deploys a fixed rule across the tested target models. GPT-style models of 120.76M/379.94M/1313.53M parameters train on 7B SlimPajama tokens with 2048 context, AdamW and three training seeds. Their fixed UDVR configurations approach the best tuned Vanilla validation perplexity and beat the tested WN/sigma-Reparam configurations, while Vanilla remains slightly stronger on LAMBADA. Additional Llama-S/OLMoE-S tests report PPL12.432/10.897 versus Vanilla12.404/10.939, with tuned Llama-S baselines but only a single reused baseline configuration for OLMoE-S. The manuscript v1 receipt is November24 16:03:02UTC; original LG NEW and dated RECENT plus official Monday14–Tuesday14/Tues20 Eastern schedule support inferred first arXiv announcement November25 01:00UTC. Earliest matching team successful catalog completion is retained. Bounded exact-title searches did not verify an earlier complete manuscript; no claim of exhaustive historical absence is made. No author code/project URL is supplied by the inspected paper.
evidence.limitations: The recipe has a substantial one-off calibration cost and retains conventional choices for parameters outside paired maps; it is not universally tuning-free. Wider small-data CIFAR transformers become unstable at the fixed C and need a lower value, and non-UDV weight decay changes sign across architectures. ImageNet results are single training seeds; language results use three seeds but small models, one short 7B-token corpus budget and limited metrics. Fixed factor norms do not imply function preservation for nonlinear FFNs, and the auxiliary scale buffer requires regularization. The SGD convergence result assumes objective-preserving rebalancing, smoothness and bounded stochastic variance; it does not prove convergence for the actual GELU/AdamW Transformer recipe. No measured wall-clock efficiency study or verified author implementation is available. OLMoE-S baseline reuse and cross-dataset muP comparisons do not establish a universal optimizer or scaling-law ranking.

entries.title: Humanity’s First Exam: Measuring the Reliability Floor of LLMs
summary: HFE tests whether language models answer elementary tasks consistently across repeated runs and controlled prompt variants, rather than merely solving one sample.
Its family-level reliability metric exposes failures hidden by high average accuracy and helps evaluation teams distinguish visual weaknesses from errors that extra reasoning can reduce.

evidence.rationale: Read all 28 pages; inspected source pages 6, 7, 9 and 18. HFE evaluates 544 prompts in 136 four-prompt families, with six rollouts per prompt, zero-shot single-turn inputs, no tools, and provider-default sampling. Equation 2 estimates all 16 selected responses being correct. Table 4’s top five configurations score 95.6–97.8% pass@1 but 80.5–92.4% family pass^4: different events, not corrected accuracy. These are static full-set paper results. The November 24 official announcement corroborates the report date; Kaggle describes a 112-prompt public subset.
evidence.limitations: Adversarial selection, model-informed quality filtering, synthetic imagery and a single Gemini grader limit interpretation. Human testing covers seeds only. Provider effort settings do not match compute, and confidence intervals are broad. This single-turn metric does not establish agent workflow reliability. No experiments were reproduced or public implementation verified.

entries.title: fork() for Agents: Agent Kernel for Non-blocking LLM Orchestration
summary: Agent-Kernel combines persistent DAG node records, dependency-aware scheduling and subgraph retry so failed branches can resume while completed siblings' text remains available to downstream agents.

Controlled transient-failure grids show full recovery where whole-trajectory replay exhausts and faster parallel execution than serial per-step retries, offering a concrete runtime design for preserving completed agent work.

evidence.rationale: Read all scientific main text, pp. 1-10, and Appendices A-Q, pp. 12-21; reference-only p. 11 was not independently audited. Directly viewed actual PDF pp. 6, 7 and 19 tables. The system stores seven-state sub-agent records and outputs in SQLite, accepts a user-declared DAG through five verbs, and dispatches a child only when all parents are complete, injecting their recorded text. An exception marks descendants unreachable; a separate bounded control loop resets the failed subgraph while preserving completed siblings. The state-preservation argument is scoped to records/outputs in this runtime, not external effects or semantic truth. The 14,434 reported runs include 11,809 core and 2,625 comparator/scaling cells, not that many independent tasks. Synthetic failures are deliberately transient: selected nodes fail only on their first attempt and succeed when retried. In Table 3, subgraph recovery is 100% versus 55% for whole-trajectory replay, but the nominal budget of three is per failed node versus per trajectory, not an equal total-call budget. Stronger serial per-step retries and the authors' Sherlock-generous adaptation also reach 100%; reported advantages over these are parallel wall-clock, with serial verifier/replay overhead confounding any general Sherlock comparison. Table 4 reports 5.5 versus 24.8 seconds on 20 AutomationBench tasks and 14.2 versus 38.1 seconds on 113 InterruptBench tasks using real Sonnet 4.5 inference; solve rates are only 5% and 44%, and latency point estimates are three-seed means without dispersion characterization. Standard linear chains have no meaningful speed gain and occasionally lower execution-completion rates from timeout tails. Broad framework comparisons are scheduling reimplementations; actual installed-binary tests cover one diamond topology, where custom-configured LangGraph also recovers fully. Prompt-mutation retry is only a small design probe, not the shipped loop: 14/18 versus 6/18 format-drift recoveries. Bounded exact-title web discovery and inspected primary links verified no matching implementation download; the manuscript supplies pseudocode, not a verified public repository. Original CL NEW membership in the Wednesday November 25 batch plus the official Tuesday 20:00 Eastern announcement schedule supports inferred November 25 01:00 UTC manuscript availability, preserving the November 24 00:33:20 submission date. This is inside the main report window. Earliest actual team discovery is the successful earlier Recipe CL RECENT completion at 11:05:16.409979 UTC, whose raw body and receipt are pinned; cross-subject appearances are not used to infer a later release.
evidence.limitations: The main failure model guarantees retryable first-attempt crashes and does not establish recovery from hallucination or capability failure. Selective DAG retry, persistence, context passing and error-feedback retry have prior lineage; this is a measured composition, not invention of subgraph recovery. Dependency correctness is synthetic/by construction and requires correct declared dependencies. The guarantee does not undo payments, file writes or messages already committed before failure, so external idempotency/transactions remain necessary. Retry scopes and comparator engineering differ; speedups are conditional on parallelism, use only the Claude family and lack characterized latency dispersion. The 100%-accuracy context-width sweep is an easy ceiling task, not general saturation evidence. Pseudocode and small structural content-plane probes do not substitute for a verified code artifact, large-scale semantic-error evaluation or independent reproduction.

entries.title: SecondChance: Benchmarking Reliable Error Recovery in AI Agents
summary: SecondChance restores agents to the same natural-error checkpoints from tau2-Bench, BFCL and AppWorld, then separately scores correction, task completion, protected state and user-facing recovery under four levels of assistance.

Across 5,760 scheduled continuations, task success can leave the original error unrepaired; the benchmark gives builders a way to distinguish completion from durable repair and measure what additional guidance accomplishes.

evidence.rationale: Read the full 18-page primary manuscript, including checkpoint selection, scoring, main results, limitations and Appendices A-G; directly inspected actual PDF pp. 6, 15 and 18 tables. Ten open-weight source models generate 4,568 valid source episodes on 487 tasks; balanced hash-ordered selection produces 129 checkpoints, not an error-prevalence sample. Four cumulative conditions supply no help, notice, location or a checkpoint-specific repair plan. Only 57 checkpoints have a demonstrated correction, 15 are proven impossible under environment assumptions, and 57 have unknown fixability. The main study schedules 5,760 continuations with one run per model/checkpoint/condition; three cells are excluded consistently in all four conditions, leaving 5,748, and 63 no-outcome jobs remain failures in their denominators. Hosted models cover the 75 tau2/BFCL checkpoints, while ten open models also cover 54 AppWorld checkpoints. Main Table 3 reports GPT-6.1-sol complete recovery at 16% unaided and 27% plan-assisted over its own population; these are not rates over all 129 checkpoints or only known-fixable errors. In AppWorld 40 of 84 task-successful continuations leave the original error. Complete recovery requires state correction/protection plus task success; user-interactive tracks additionally require policy compliance, no false claims, the user goal and disclosure. Disclosure after correction is allowed in the main definition, while separate stricter consent-first readings remove some acceptances. Semantic judgment uses pinned Qwen3-235B with evidence rechecks and author adjudication, with only ten cases independently human-audited. Cluster bootstrap resamples source tasks, retaining paired conditions/repetitions. The complete HF release has reachable commit b445642c5d381a36709a7ee057f7aaecc210c30e dated November 23 21:06:41 UTC, before the manuscript submission at 21:31:29 that day. Its immutable card already describes all checkpoints, main/supporting continuations, outcomes and the paper-table reconstruction protocol; original November 23 publication is retained and this is a delayed discovery within the exact 72-hour window. Git/HF metadata does not prove the exact instant of historical public visibility, so no exact public-availability timestamp is invented. The Wednesday November 25 original CL batch establishes the later manuscript announcement, not a new benchmark release. Earliest timestamped team discovery is Recipe's successful CL RECENT completion today at 11:05:16.409979 UTC, copied and hash-pinned. The actual HF dataset page/API/card are HTTP 200, but the claimed GitHub harness landing and API/history are HTTP 404; no working code release or independent reproduction is claimed.
evidence.limitations: Selected simulated state-changing errors are not real-world failure prevalence and may miss earlier non-state mistakes. Unknown fixability is not impossibility, and a demonstrated correction need not make full task completion reachable. The main study has one run per cell; three-sample controls cover only 37 simpler tau2/BFCL checkpoints. Hosted coverage is one provider with an undated GPT-6.1-sol alias, AppWorld is open-model-only, public tasks may have been seen in training, and model populations differ. Human semantic validation covers only ten cases; acknowledgment lacks human validation, and disclosure/consent choices change acceptance rates. Source-user simulation and per-environment budgets are part of the measured system. HF provides annotations/results, but AppWorld histories/state/targets are omitted under its distribution restrictions, and the linked GitHub harness is unavailable. No author code was executed and no experiments were independently reproduced.

entries.title: Generalized Tensor Parallelism: New Scaling and Training Evaluation of an Existing Runtime
summary: This new study evaluates Megatron-Core’s existing generalized tensor parallelism, which treats weight and activation sharding as separate choices and schedules weight transfers around individual matrix multiplications.
Consumer-specific waits and separate prefetch chains help hide communication while controlling temporary memory, giving builders a concrete framework for configuring very large training jobs.
The authors report 13.0 model EFLOP/s on 12,288 GB300 GPUs, although the smaller matched comparisons show important microbatch, memory and baseline-dependent tradeoffs.

evidence.rationale: Read the complete scientific main text, pages 1–33 and the page 34 pre-reference conclusion/acknowledgments of the 40-page manuscript, including implementation, all evaluation sections and configuration limits; references run from pages 34–40. Original source pages 21, 24 and 27 were visually inspected. This is the newly disclosed quantitative manuscript study of an existing runtime. The immutable November 19 guide is byte-identical to today’s 119 KB documentation and already explains GTP, consumer-level rematerialization and an older approximately 280B-parameter GB200 study on 128–3,072 GPUs. The new paper instead provides the full Internal-2T GB300 study, the 1T-token Nemotron-3-Nano comparison, matched FSDP/3D studies and component ablations. At 8K sequences, PP1/MBS1, eager Muon and no forced routing balance, Internal-2T reaches 13.03 model EFLOP/s on 12,288 GB300 GPUs, with 98.2% weak-scaling efficiency from 4,096 GPUs; fixed-batch strong-scaling efficiency is 91.7%. Model FLOPs exclude recomputation and are not physical peak throughput. Smaller 256–1,024-GPU MXFP8 comparisons match model, global batch, sequence length and recomputation/offloading policies: GTP is 1.05–1.55× evaluated Megatron-FSDP, but only 1.04× PyTorch FSDP2 in the matched 256-GPU DSV3-proxy comparison, using 183 versus 219 GB/GPU. Against tuned 3D parallelism on the DSV4-Pro proxy, separately chosen microbatches give 1.27–1.31× throughput at 29–48% higher memory use; at matched microbatch size 1, GTP is slower. Separate mechanism ablations and the 1T-token MXFP8 AdamW loss comparison support the reported mechanism. The original v1 receipt is November 24 at 06:45:36 UTC; the original Wednesday November 25 DC batch and official announcement schedule infer public paper availability at November 25, 01:00 UTC. The earliest verified matching team catalog completion is retained. The implementation landing, immutable source tree and source file were retrieved, without execution.
evidence.limitations: The implementation and many mechanisms predate this window; novelty is the new study. Most performance tests use random initialization, forced routing balance, MXFP8 and selected development software on GB300; the large scale-out run is a distinct Muon/eager configuration. Baseline expert sharding, alignment fallback, module grouping, stage imbalance and separately tuned microbatches affect comparisons. The FSDP2 gain is modest and does not isolate one change. The quality comparison uses 31.6B-total/3.2B-active Nemotron-3-Nano with differing GPU/parallel layouts, rather than a trained-to-convergence 2T model or bitwise layout invariance. The Muon loss curve has no matched baseline. Larger global batches narrow the pipeline advantage; padding and communication can erase memory gains, and pipeline parallelism can remain useful. Some ablations and Muon points are single-run; small differences lack repeated-run uncertainty. No experiments or author code were independently executed.

entries.title: Norn: Context-Length-Aware Optimization of Weight and KV Cache Placement for Offloaded LLM Inference
summary: Norn precomputes CPU/GPU execution plans and switches weight and KV-cache placement as a request’s context grows, without requiring its output length in advance.
It also processes prompt chunks by sublayer to reuse transferred weights, helping memory-constrained desktop inference balance weight residency, cache growth and PCIe traffic.

On two single-GPU systems it reduces end-to-end latency by up to 4.2× versus an output-length-aware Pipelined Sharding oracle, with batch-one dummy-input evaluation and substantial offline planning costs.

evidence.rationale: Read the complete scientific main text, pages 1–10 of the 13-page paper; pages 11–13 are references and there are no appendices. Original source pages 8–10 were visually inspected. Offline profiling measures compute, transfer and contention; a mixed-integer linear program chooses counts of eight attention/FFN modes, followed by simulation and heuristic assignment across layers. The planner scans context ranges from long to short, uses 5%/10% degradation thresholds, and adjusts or merges boundaries with migration costs. Optimal MILP subproblems do not make the combined planner globally optimal. Runtime switches at token boundaries; operator-major chunked prefill retains full-input hidden states to avoid reloading weights for every chunk. FP16 Qwen3-14B/32B tests use batch 1, greedy decoding, fixed output lengths and dummy inputs: RTX 5090 with 32 GiB, Core Ultra 7 265K and PCIe 5×16, or RTX 3090 Ti with 24 GiB, i9-10980XE and PCIe 3×16; each has 128 GiB RAM and eight CPU threads. For 1K–128K inputs with 32-token outputs, end-to-end latency improves by up to 16.8× over Pipelined Sharding fixed at 128K capacity and up to 4.2× over PS-O, which knows input and output lengths. In the longer-output sweeps, average time per output token beats PS-O in 16 of 24 cells, including all eight 16K-output cases, but is up to 5.8% slower in some short-output cells. Planning takes 245–2,081 seconds for 2–27 final plans, outside request latency. Switching spikes and prefill-to-decode transfers are separately discussed. The v1 receipt is November 24 at 09:55:02 UTC; original Wednesday November 25 DC batch membership and the official schedule infer paper announcement at November 25, 01:00 UTC. No author implementation was verified: the linked Zenodo/GitHub artifact is the older Pipelined Sharding baseline, rather than Norn code.
evidence.limitations: Only two dense Qwen models, two desktop systems, batch 1 and synthetic fixed-length inputs are evaluated. The 16.8× headline partly reflects a fixed 128K-capacity baseline; the stronger output-length-aware oracle sometimes wins. No standard serving-engine, concurrent-request, quality, stochastic-generation or production-workload evaluation is supplied. Although the method does not quantize and is called lossless, heterogeneous CPU/GPU execution is not demonstrated to be bitwise identical or semantically equivalent. Offline profiling and planning need amortization and stable hardware/contention. Heuristic plans incur migration latency spikes. The PyTorch/Transformers implementation and llama.cpp-based comparator differ, so gains bundle planner, placement, prefill and backend choices. Repeat counts and statistical uncertainty are not clearly specified. Author code was not verified.

entries.title: Joule is FLOP: Optimizing Tensor-Core Kernels Beyond Latency Hiding at the GPU Power Wall
summary: Joule models how data movement consumes energy even when its latency is hidden, reducing the clock that a power-capped GPU can sustain.
It uses that model to guide wider tensor-core tiles, asynchronous accumulator reuse and power-aware work placement, connecting kernel design to energy and runtime rather than cycle counts alone.

The tested low-precision GEMMs improve geometric-mean speed by 2.12–6.64% over exhaustively selected cuBLAS algorithms on three GPUs; these are kernel measurements requiring device- and input-specific calibration.

evidence.rationale: Read the full scientific main text, pages 1–11 and the page 12 pre-reference conclusion/acknowledgments of the 14-page paper; there are no scientific appendices. Original source pages 8 and 9 were visually inspected. A calibrated physical-path event-energy model incorporates nonlinear voltage/frequency curves and solves for the steady-state clock under a power cap. Its conditional data-movement bounds are modeled ceilings, rather than universal measured hardware limits. On B200, wide tiles use two accumulator panels and a rotated K-block order with early release to overlap epilogue readout; a CPU scheduler coordinates die-local placement, variable widths, read sharing and cache traversal. Low-precision dense tests cover 60 layer shapes from five Qwen3 models at 2K, 4K, 8K and 16K token counts: MXFP8 on B200 at 1,000 W and RTX PRO 6000 at 600 W, and 1×128 FP8 on H100 NVL at 400 W, using CUDA 13.4 and cuBLAS 13.1. Each point is the median of three 3-second CUDA-graph runs after a 45°C cooldown, discarding the initial second and flushing L2. Geometric-mean speedups over per-shape exhaustive cuBLAS selection are 4.94%, 6.64% and 2.12%, respectively; separate BF16 suites are also reported. B200 without caller-side die-local placement still improves by 4.25%, versus 4.94% with placement. Given measured event counts, held-out-family energy error on B200 is 0.69%, distinct from analytical event estimation for candidate selection. Fused DeepSeek-V4-Pro Mega-MoE on eight B200 GPUs gains 2.60–5.17% over upstream DeepGEMM with die-local expert weights. The original v1 receipt is November 24 at 11:40:37 UTC; the original Wednesday November 25 DC batch and official schedule infer paper announcement at November 25, 01:00 UTC. The paper promises later open sourcing; no author implementation was verified by its links or bounded repository search.
evidence.limitations: The method applies to steady-state kernels near their board power cap with meaningful reducible traffic. Per-device coefficients, voltage curves and the target operand-value distribution require calibration; another card of the same model still needs fitting. Profiling counters perturb power, so event collection and steady-state measurements use separate passes. The 0.69% energy error assumes measured event counts and must not be presented as end-to-end error without profiling. Some 2K-token shapes regress; there is no whole-model latency, quality or convergence evaluation. Caller-side die placement constrains portability. MoE accumulation order differs from upstream even though each implementation is batch invariant. Timing repeats do not establish deployment-wide robustness. Author code was not verified and no results were independently reproduced.
